question: GQ-001
subject: four title rules chased one archive; the identifier prefix caught it in one
the_pattern_of_my_own_errors: I wrote FOUR title rules — correspondence, street address, court filing, photo view-note — and each removed one shape of the same collection and revealed the next. The fifth batch still failed 17 of 27 with "Colonial Bungalow, Flintridge, California": a house photograph with no view-note parenthetical, so rule four missed it.

the_signal_i_should_have_looked_for_firs.method: group every NO_TEXT failure across all manifests by IDENTIFIER PREFIX
the_signal_i_should_have_looked_for_firs.caggljhs: 13 usable of 100 attempted (13%) — and all 13 are OCR of handwriting, already excluded
the_signal_i_should_have_looked_for_firs.why_it_is_stronger: a title describes an ITEM; a prefix describes the SOURCE, and the source is what has no text layer

the_fix: an empirical barren-collection block, learned from measured outcomes rather than guessed from titles. Each prefix is listed with its success rate over 100+ real attempts, so a collection that starts producing text can be re-checked against recorded evidence.

result.ninth_list: complete — 440 of 441 eligible already on vault

the_lesson: when a filter needs a fourth special case, the taxonomy is wrong. Four title patterns were four descriptions of one archive; one prefix was the archive.
